summary: Plan and EXECUTION-CONTRACT.md written, then WIDENED 2026-08-12 on operator direction from 2 changes to 5 across two file-disjoint tracks. Track A (identity/tenancy): gap-02 then gap-03, strictly serial. Track B (skills): skill-builtins-on-embedded, skill-scoped-governance, skill-config-reconciliation, strictly serial. Track B replaces the held GAP-05: grounding showed SPECIFICATION.md:445 wrong in three ways and disproved the contract's own earlier claim that builtins are in-memory only - commit fdd69a2f made register persist via db.save_skill (registry.rs:69-99). The real defect is that embedded.rs never calls the builtin loader, so a FRESH embedded database gets no builtins. Operator decisions recorded: builtins durable and non-deletable; all skills configurable at global/agent/conversation with live effect; config reconciles into DB at startup; removal is tombstone-with-restore, never hard delete. skill-scoped-governance supersedes fix-skills-scope-semantics and adopts its skill-governance capability name. provider_id (fs-skills/builtin/api/wasm) is the existing discriminator that makes reconciliation safe - no schema change needed. All five changes validate --strict.
parallel: Track A and Track B are file-disjoint
openItems: add-skill-kind-and-origin has 3 tasks left (8/11); defines SkillOrigin that Track B consumes
risks: R-4 unmitigated: overlap scan covered only security/a2a/skill-registration terms across ~190 active changes
R-6 data loss: B5 could tombstone a user-created skill if provider_id is unreliable in some path. Stop condition 9 plus negative control B5 task 4.8
R-7 B4 supersedes an unstarted change authored by someone else
